relevance_note: The paper describes three patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variants and their carrier parents, e.g. 'He had a heterozygous c.574G>A (p.Glu192Lys) variant of TNFAIP3.'
method_note: Read the paper in full and built the JSON with a short Python script in my scratch directory; every value was typed from my reading, no table was machine-transcribed. Table 1 has patients as columns (header 'Patient no.' with sub-row P1/P2/P3); spans quote the row from its label through the patient's cell. Labels: the text uses 'Patient 1/2/3' more often than the table's 'P1/P2/P3', so rule 1 gives 'Patient 1' etc. Relatives: 'father of Patient 1', 'mother of Patient 2', 'father of Patient 3'. The other parent in each family was sequenced ('Sanger sequencing was performed for the patients and their parents'; WES of 'patient 3 and her parents') but no result or individual detail is given, so they get no rows; P3's mother's result is not stated. is_proband left null for the three patients: the paper never calls them proband/index case and it is not a single-patient case report. cohort_size_as_stated = 3 (the three patients studied); P1's variant was found 'among 55 patients suspected of having autoinflammatory diseases analyzed at Gifu University Hospital', while P2 and P3 were recruited from collaborators, so 55 is a screening denominator for one patient only, not the study size. Parental zygosity 'heterozygous' rests on 'the same variant' plus the Fig. 1 legend 'Pedigree of the families with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants'. Inheritance (paternal/maternal) follows v4 D-24 from the stated carrier parent. No transcript is printed for any variant (Supplementary Table S2 gives NP_001257437.1 only as the protein used for an alignment), so transcript is 'not reported'. ACMG criteria codes are not printed. MEFV c.329T>C and c.442G>C are recorded for Patient 2 (attributed to her; not dismissed as benign by the authors). Previously published variants (Cys243Tyr, Met476Ile, Thr647Pro, Lys417Serfs*4), the SNP Phe127Cys and somatic/COSMIC Gln709His are used only as assay controls or literature with no individual-level patient facts, so no rows. Table 1 'Autoantibody | No' for P1 and P2 is a word, not a symbol, and is taken as explicit absence. Supplementary Table S1 (flow cytometry): only values marked with arrows (defined in the legend as higher/lower than the normal range) were recorded as observed features; columns are normal range 2-6 y, P1, normal range >=20 y, P2, P3. Possible inconsistencies: (1) Patient 2 had 'a high level of serum CRP' with attacks, but 'Serum inflammatory reactants were negative during the intermittent episodes of fever'; I read the latter as between attacks, recorded both rows, and kept the checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers' observed. (2) Patient 1 'had no abnormalities in ... lymphocyte fraction' at initial work-up, while Supplementary Table S1 shows decreased T cells (42.6 ↓) at the time of analysis; both recorded, likely different time points. (3) Text gives P2's onset of abdominal pain 'around the age of 12' and recurrent fever 'Around 13 years of age'; Table 1 onset '12 y' was used for the person-level onset. Checklist choices: P1 'temporary nonbacterial coxitis' -> arthritis observed; P1 cervical lymphadenitis -> lymphadenopathy observed; P1 repeated tonsillitis/bronchitis with no pathogens detected -> recurrent infections left 'not reported'; P3 single fever at 24 y -> recurrent fever 'not reported'; P3 facial erythema -> skin lesions observed; P3 athetoid cerebral palsy (after neonatal cardiopulmonary arrest) and epilepsy -> CNS involvement observed; father of P1 'recurrent stomatitis' not mapped to oral ulcers (stomatitis is not stated to be ulcerative); asymptomatic carrier parents ('lacked any symptoms') have one excluded feature row each but all checklist items 'not reported', since the blanket statement names no feature. Age at diagnosis left 'not reported' for all: Table 1 'Age of analysis' is ambiguous (flow cytometry/genetic analysis) and was not used; the text ages (4-, 20-, 24-year-old) were used as age at last evaluation. Spans and verbatim values keep the paper's thin spaces (U+2009) and non-breaking spaces (U+00A0); a script matched each span to the paper text with flexible whitespace and copied the exact characters (whitespace-only changes, reviewed).

The variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, Gln709Arg, and Cys243Tyr did not show differences in deubiquitination from the WT (Fig. 5).
